verdicts.summary:
Lean has a stronger form of it. (1.2) is the forced incompressible Euler system, given as background in §1.1 "Historical context and previous work". In the text layer "(1.2)", "D t u" and "Newton" occur only on p. 2, and "Euler" only on p. 2 and in the bibliography (p. 165), so nothing later in the paper relies on the display.

The in-scope tree never writes the Euler system out. A case-insensitive grep for "euler" over NavierStokes/ and NavierStokes.lean returns nothing, no `navierStokesResidual 0` occurs, and no declaration names the material acceleration D_t. What the tree states is the momentum equation as a family in the viscosity: `NavierStokesR3.ProblemStatement.navierStokesResidual ν u p t x = f (t, x)` with ν an unconstrained real, together with `spatialDivergence u t x = 0`. Both appear as fields of `CandidateProperties ν` and `GlobalFiniteEnergySolution ν`, with no positivity hypothesis on ν. `0 < ν` appears only in `coreBreakdownStatement` and `breakdownStatement`.

From Lean to the display: set ν := 0 and unfold to get `temporalDerivative u t x + advection u t x - 0 • spatialLaplacian u t x + pressureGradient p t x = f (t, x)`. Then `zero_smul`, `sub_zero` and moving the gradient across give ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p + f with the paper's signs. The clause ∇·u = 0 is the `divergence_free` field verbatim. These are specialisation, unfolding and algebra, so the step is formal and needs no analytic fact.

From the display to Lean: the stated Lean formula is the whole ν-family, and the Euler system does not give the term −ν • spatialLaplacian for general ν (that term is display (1.1)). No declaration states the ν = 0 instance on its own. So the two are not equivalent; the Lean definition is strictly more general.

The Lean fields carry time ranges (Ioo 0 1 / Ico 0 1, Ioi 0 / Ici 0) that the display, which has no ranges, does not specify. D_t u is notation only; its content `temporalDerivative u t x + advection u t x` is the leading subterm of the residual and has no name of its own in the tree.
